## Semantic policies

- Constant folding: `compiler_evaluates_the_same_canonical_rule_and_reason_codes_used_by_runtime_lowering`
- Runtime lowering: `both_backends_lower_only_from_serialized_canonical_conversion_kind_width_signedness_and_policy`
- Out of range: `checked_numeric_rejects_with_conversion_out_of_range_truncate_and_wrapping_require_explicit_policy`
- Negative to unsigned: `checked_conversion_rejects_with_conversion_negative_to_unsigned_wrapping_requires_explicit_policy`
- Unsigned to signed: `checked_conversion_rejects_out_of_range_with_conversion_unsigned_to_signed_out_of_range`
- Pointer-sized widths: `isize_and_usize_width_is_selected_from_the_declared_target_pointer_width_before_rule_selection`

## Boundary

pointer_integer_conversion_remains_deferred_to_pointer_policy_floating_point_conversion_outside_patch

MIR-to-C and Cranelift consume the same compiler-selected conversion kind, widths, signedness, policy, target identity, and stable reason codes. Neither backend is the semantic authority.
